scenes.narration: Day three. Someone is knocking on the back door of the pharmacy. Open it?
scenes.visual: back door, knocking, OPEN IT? card

scenes.narration: Three nights ago, you were just working the night shift. Small town. Twenty-four hour pharmacy. Nothing ever happens.
scenes.visual: calm pharmacy interior at night, you behind the counter

scenes.narration: Your little sister Mia was doing her homework at the counter. Seven years old. Waiting for you to drive her home.
scenes.visual: Mia at the counter with a notebook

scenes.narration: At two in the morning, every phone in the store started screaming at once.
scenes.visual: phones lighting up with EMERGENCY ALERT

scenes.narration: The radio said stay inside. Lock your doors. Do not let anyone in... no matter what they say.
scenes.visual: radio on the counter, alert text

scenes.narration: Then you saw them. In the parking lot. Walking wrong. Too slow... then way too fast.
scenes.visual: shambling figures in the parking lot under a streetlight

scenes.narration: You hit the button for the metal shutter. It comes down so slowly. Inches from the ground... something slams into it.
scenes.visual: roll-down shutter closing, a hand hits it

scenes.narration: Since then, it's been you, Mia, and twenty aisles of cold medicine and candy bars.
scenes.visual: you and Mia sitting between shelves

scenes.narration: You've got food. Chips. Crackers. Enough for weeks.
But on day two... the taps stopped working.
The fridge had eleven bottles of water. Now it has two.
And tonight, someone is at the back door. Knocking. Calm. Three knocks... every minute.
Then a voice. Please. I'm not sick. I have water.
scenes.visual: the door, a shadow under it

scenes.narration: Mia looks at you. You look at the door.
Open it? Tell me in the comments... part two is up next.
